edges.reason: msg.sender is written into the owner state variable in the constructor, establishing privileged authority.
diamondCut authorizes the caller with require(msg.sender == owner), so caller identity controls execution of privileged logic.
Because only the owner can pass the msg.sender check, the caller identity gates the arbitrary delegatecall to _init.
The selector parameter is written into selectorToAddress by addSelector.
The facet address parameter is appended to addressToSelectors[facetAddress_] in addSelector.
The caller-supplied _init address is the delegatecall target, allowing arbitrary code execution in the contract context.
The caller-supplied _calldata bytes are forwarded directly to the delegatecall.
The facet address resolved from selectorToAddress[msg.sig] becomes the delegatecall target in the fallback.
Each element of the _diamondCut array is copied into the memory local facetCut.
The fallback reads selectorToAddress[msg.sig] into the local address_ before delegating.
The fallback function's assembly block always reaches the delegatecall.
diamondCut conditionally performs the delegatecall to _init when _init is non-zero.
diamondCut calls facetAddressExists to decide whether a new facet address must be registered.
diamondCut dispatches to addSelector when the action is FacetCutAction.Add.
diamondCut dispatches to removeSelector when the action is FacetCutAction.Remove.
diamondCut dispatches to replaceSelector when the action is FacetCutAction.Replace.
The delegatecall in the fallback executes external facet code in this contract's context, which can re-enter the fallback or any registered selector.
The delegatecall to _init runs external code with the diamond's storage, allowing re-entry into diamondCut before the event is emitted.
